Side spin grips the cushion as the ball turns off it. Spin that turns the same way the ball runs along the rail pushes it on along the rail, so it leaves at a wider angle than it came in.

The cushion's grip can change the ball's speed along the rail by at most the grip times one plus the bounce, times the speed straight into the rail. Running side spends that push speeding the ball along the rail, so it leaves at a wider angle than it came in.
